transcript.text: dryer drum wont turn but i can here it running, hotpiont. clothes just sit there

That sound of a running motor while the drum stays still usually points to the drive belt having snapped or slipped off its pulleys. It could also be the tensioner pulley that keeps the belt tight, but a broken belt is the most common cause. To confirm this safely, please unplug the dryer first. Then with the drum empty, try turning it by hand. If it spins around very easily with no resistance at all (like it's disconnected), the belt is almost certainly off or snapped. If it feels stiff or hard to turn, that suggests a different issue like a seized bearing. What does it feel like when you turn it by hand?
just tried it unplugged and the drum spins really easy, almost no resistance at all

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
That confirms the drive belt has either snapped or slipped off its pulleys. To fix this, you will need to replace the drive belt. This usually involves removing the top panel and then the front or rear panel of the dryer to access the drum and motor. Since this requires dismantling the appliance casing, I recommend checking if your Hotpoint model has a specific service manual available online, or contacting a qualified engineer to perform the repair safely.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
i can take the back panel off myself got a screwdriver set. only know the model starts TVHM8 the rest of the sticker is worn off. how do i get to the belt

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
Accessing it from the back is often easier than the front on many Hotpoint models. Please unplug the dryer again for safety. Remove the screws securing the rear panel and lift it away. Look inside at the large drum pulley: you should see a black rubber belt looped around it. If it's not there, or if it has slipped down onto the smaller motor shaft, that confirms the fault. Also check the small plastic tensioner wheel (jockey pulley) to ensure it hasn't broken. Once you've checked this, let me know exactly what you see (belt on drum, belt on motor, or no belt at all) and whether the tensioner wheel is intact. I can then guide you through removing the old belt and fitting a new one.
got the back off and theres no belt on the drum, just a black rubbery strip lying at the bottom. not sure about the tensioner wheel, how do i tell if its ok

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
That confirms the drive belt has snapped or slipped off. To ensure a new belt will work correctly, we need to check the tensioner (jockey pulley) that keeps it tight. Look for a small plastic wheel on a spring-loaded arm near the motor. Is the wheel still attached to its arm? If you spin it by hand, does it turn smoothly or is it stiff/wobbly?
not sure where the tensioner is exactly, whats it look like. ive got the back off and can see the motor, will have a look

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
This is the tensioner (jockey pulley). If the wheel is broken or stuck, it needs replacing along with the belt. If it looks fine, we can proceed with fitting a new belt.

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
The tensioner (jockey pulley) is a small plastic wheel mounted on a metal arm with a spring. It sits near the motor and pushes against the belt to keep it tight. On many Hotpoint dryers, it is located at the bottom of the motor assembly. Look for this small wheel; if it is broken or stuck, you will need to replace it along with the belt. Once you have cleared out any debris, you can proceed with installing the new belt. If you find the tensioner wheel is also broken or stiff, replace it at the same time.
ok ill have a look near the motor with the torch. how do i get the new belt on once i have one

[Heading: Drive belt failure]
Since you have the back panel off and can see the motor, fitting a new belt is straightforward. First, loop the new belt around the large pulley on the drum. Next, stretch it over the smaller shaft on the motor. Finally, route the belt under the tensioner (jockey) wheel to take up any slack; you may need to push the tensioner arm slightly against its spring to get the last bit of belt on. Once it is seated correctly on all three components, replace the back panel and test.
